artists.biography: The League of Gentlemen is a British surreal comedy horror series that premiered on BBC Two in 1999. The programme is set in Royston Vasey, a fictional town in northern England, and follows the lives of bizarre characters, most of whom are played by three of the show's four writers—Mark Gatiss, Steve Pemberton, and Reece Shearsmith—who, along with Jeremy Dyson, formed the League of Gentlemen comedy troupe in 1995. The series originally aired for three series from 1999 until 2002, and was followed by a film The League of Gentlemen's Apocalypse (2005), a stage production The League of Gentlemen Are Behind You! (2005), and another live show, The League of Gentlemen Live Again! (2018)

perplexity.description:
Live Again!" is a live album by The League of Gentlemen, released in 2019 by Demon Records. The album captures the group's stage show of the same name, which marked their return to live performance after a long hiatus. Musically, the album blends dark comedy, character-driven sketches, and theatrical elements, reflecting the troupe's roots in stage and screen. The performances feature a mix of classic characters and new material, delivered with the group's signature blend of macabre humor and musical interludes, making it a distinctive entry in their discography.

As the first major live release since their earlier stage productions, "Live Again!" holds a significant place in The League of Gentlemen's body of work, bridging their television legacy with their live theatrical output. The album was well-received by fans and critics for its energy, nostalgic value, and the seamless integration of comedy and music. Its release coincided with a renewed interest in the group, following their 20th-anniversary television specials, and it stands as a testament to their enduring appeal in the realm of British comedy and stage performance.
